art.title: A Young Woman Reading
art.why: A woman reading a book, propped on one elbow on a grassy bank: an ordinary reader, reading slowly. (Outdoors, not by a window: the window readers were claimed.)
Jerome at a desk: the free Jeromes are claimed (Veronese workshop by guilt-and-forgiveness) or have no gallery description (Benaglio), so they cannot be described.
No Lamb of God or Fountain of Life in the NGA open data.
No Church Fathers or disputation free (both Christ among the Doctors panels are used).
Preacher or congregation: Daumier's In Church is claimed by reformation; Catlin's Kickapoo preaching has no gallery description.
Monk reading: A Miracle of Saint Benedict (French 15th c.) is claimed by fall-of-rome; Bellini's and Cima's Jeromes are used.

Saint Anthony: osservanza-anthony-alms (Antony giving away his goods, exactly Life of Antony 2) is already used by good-life and the-poor; Jacopo Bellini's Anthony is claimed by dostoevsky. Reuse osservanza-anthony-alms only if the lead agent allows a third use.

music.why: 'This place was made by God': a short motet to begin a habit in a quiet place.
Byrd wrote this Mass for Catholics worshipping in secret: words set so plainly that every syllable is heard.
The Mass said to have shown the Council of Trent that polyphony could keep the words clear: layers of meaning that never drown the text.
Augustine's rule is that every reading must build up love; this chant says where love is, God is.
A spiritual made by enslaved people who read the same Bible their enslavers misused, and found the cross in it.
Psalm 51, prayed slowly: Scripture turned into prayer, as lectio teaches.
A chorale for a daily habit: steady, unhurried, joyful.
